pattern_id: Probe state can set Next < Match violating Raft invariant due to delayed message handling
description: BUG PATTERN: Probe state can set Next index less than Match, violating Raft invariant. DESCRIPTION: In MaybeDecrTo() for probe state, the code pr.Next = max(min(rejected, matchHint+1), 1) can set Next < Match. The code checks pr.Next-1 != rejected to detect stale responses, assuming only one probe is in flight (where Next-1 == Match). But messages can be delayed, reordered, or duplicated, breaking this assumption. A delayed rejected probe response received when leader enters another probe state can corrupt the progress tracking. ROOT CAUSE: The probe state logic assumes single-probe-in-flight but network can deliver old responses later. The staleness check uses Next-1 instead of Match, which is only equivalent under the single-probe assumption. When multiple delayed responses exist, the wrong check allows Next to go below Match. LESSON: In Raft progress tracking: 1) Always check invariants (Next > Match) explicitly, not via proxy conditions; 2) Network can delay/reorder/duplicate any message - design for this; 3) Assumptions like 'only one message in flight' are fragile; 4) The StateReplicate branch correctly checks against Match - probe should too; 5) Test with message delays, reordering, and duplication scenarios.
